title: Remove the stale duplicate preview root and inspect skinning weights by posing limbs
description:
## Summary
Remove the stale duplicate creature preview root from the Test scene after proving regeneration is available, then test limb posing through MCP and inspect the skinning weights numerically and visually.

## User Mandate
> "you have the right to remove the duplicate preview if you can regenerate (you need to have a way to do so if you can't already . do some more tests and try rotating the limbs and taking pictures to inspect the animation weight"

STRICT. Binding constraints:
- Removing the duplicate is conditional on regeneration being possible.
- If regeneration is not possible, create that capability first.
- Rotate limbs and capture pictures to inspect animation weights.

## Scope
- `Assets/Test.unity`: deleted the orphan root `CreatureCreator Preview 2 (1)`; scene saved.
- No production code, DNA, or test changes.
- Skinning evidence captured under `Assets/Screenshots/`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Regeneration availability is proven, not assumed.
- The removed duplicate is confirmed non-owned before deletion.
- Limb rotation produces visible deformation and captures.
- Weight findings are reported with numbers, not impressions.

## Validation
- Ownership proof: `SessionState["ProceduralCreature.Editor.Preview.RootEntityId"] = 568105589213148736` matches `CreatureCreator Preview`; the deleted root carried entity id `568105584918897610`, absent from the session keys, so it was an unowned orphan from an earlier editor session. The orphan contained a doubled rig (2 bone roots plus 2 skinned meshes).
- Regeneration proof: `CreatureEditorWindow` exposes a `Regenerate Preview` toolbar button (`CreatureEditorWindow.cs:460`), auto-regenerates after definition edits (`ScheduleAutoRegeneration` to `ProcessAutoRegeneration`, lines 3210-3249), and recovers its root through `CreaturePreviewController.RecoverExistingPreview()` on reload. No new regeneration capability was required.
- Weight statistics over 8,118 vertices: influences 1=556, 2=3785, 3=3531, 4=246; zero vertices with weight sum outside 1.0000; per-bone counts recorded.
- Isolated 45-degree bone probes measuring baked vertex displacement: front knee j1 567 moved / max 0.7950; front knee j2 567 / 0.7945; front foot 129 / 0.1900; hind knee j1 842 / 1.0227; hind knee j2 842 / 0.3558; hind foot 233 / 0.1755; tail_2 1262 / 1.7610; tail_3 716 / 1.1484; head 517 / 0.0953; spine_2 776 / 0.6615.
- Captures: `screenshot-20260912-021242.png` (single-joint front-knee bend, three-quarter), a 6-angle contact sheet of a combined dynamic pose, and `screenshot-20260912-021339.png` (rest restore) plus the earlier baseline sheet.
- Rest restore verified exact: all 34 bones restored, worst deviation 0.0000 degrees, `scene.isDirty == False`.
- `read_console(types=["error","warning"])`: no C# errors; one `Command TCS timed out` bridge warning.

## Findings
- Deformation locality is clean: each joint moves only its own influence set, and parent rotations move exactly their subtree union (j1 and j2 both move 567), with no global motion.
- Four rig bones influence zero vertices: `Bone_part_64d046b5`, `Bone_part_64d046b5_mirror`, `Bone_part_9b22a26a`, and `_mirror`. Both were probed at 45 degrees and moved 0 of 8,118 vertices, confirming dead bones near the head.
- Weighting is diffuse at the head: `Bone_body_head` has 538 influenced vertices but a maximum weight of only 0.447, and a 45-degree rotation moves its vertices only 0.0953 units. Head articulation is soft rather than rigid.
- Small pale shard islands remain detached near the head in both rest and posed captures. They are a pre-existing mesh artifact, not a weight artifact, but they do not visibly follow the head.
- `RigSkinningSweepDiagnostic` could not run: it validates on `RestSkeleton != null && IndexedBones.Count > 0`, and the live `CreatureRig` was unbuilt (`Bones.Count == 0`). `EditorApplication.ExecuteMenuItem` returned `false`. The rig is runtime-only state that a domain reload discards while the preview root persists in the saved scene.

## Blockers
None for this scope. The sweep diagnostic is blocked until the preview is regenerated in-session; tracked separately.

## Next Step
Give agents a non-UI way to regenerate the preview so the rig is rebuilt and the skinning sweep becomes reachable. Also consider pruning dead rig bones and investigating the detached head shards.
